subject: Customers report tail latency & 502 spike — potential peering/DNS + corporate-proxy path
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@citrine.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Citrine SRE <sre@citrine.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency + 502 spike from our users — noticed after 08:45 PDT

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

We're seeing a sudden cluster of 502s and tail latencies in our production traffic starting ~08:45 PDT today. Error rate on our inference calls climbed from ~0.5% to ~7% over the 20m window; p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s. This is impacting the checkout flow for several enterprise users.

We ran quick checks:
- Increased 502s correlate with requests routed to us-east-1 nodes.
- Traceroutes show occasional detours through an unfamiliar proxy hop within the customer path (we've attached a small pcap and the sampled query log).
- DNS resolution for inference.redwood.com sometimes resolves to a different egress IP for a subset of prefixes.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing any peering anomalies or if there are recent firewall/proxy changes on the egress path? Our SREs can keep digging but wanted to alert you immediately so we can coordinate.

Attachments: pcap_snapshot_20270914.zip, citrine_query_log_0914.csv

Thanks,
Alex Kim
Sr. Platform Engineer | Citrine Labs
--
On behalf of Citrine SRE team
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@citrine.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency + 502 spike from our users — noticed after 08:45 PDT

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the pcap/logs.

We're pulling telemetry now. Initial notes:
- We see matching 502 surge from our front-door in us-east-1 between 08:44–09:05 PDT, traffic with similar source ASN patterns (customer prefixes).
- There are sporadic DNS resolution differences for inference.redwood.com in a small subset of recursive resolvers — looks like inconsistent TTLs + a cached response pointing at an older egress IP.
- Ben is running a quick health check on the us-east peering cluster; Vivek is checking whether recent firewall rules or proxy routing updates were applied that could introduce a mid-path proxy.

Immediate plan:
1) Ben to validate peering health + route announcements and share any ASN/next-hop anomalies (ETA 20m).
2) Vivek to confirm firewall/proxy rule changes and any ACL rollouts in the past 24h (ETA 30m).
3) I'll request that our edge auto-fallback remove the suspect egress IP from rotation for a short canary window if we can replicate.

We will keep you posted and loop in execs if remediation looks like it will take >2h.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@citrine.ai>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency + 502 spike from our users — potential peering issue

Quick findings from peering and route telemetry:
- Route announcements to us-east-1 show transient withdrawal from one of our secondary peers (peer-22) between 08:42–08:49 PDT which aligns with the onset.
- That withdrawal caused a subset of prefixes to be pulled across an alternative transit that appears to include a corporate proxy hop (we're seeing an extra AS path hop: 396531 -> 64512 -> 1337).
- Packet keeps alive / healthchecks to the suspect egress IP show occasional TCP RSTs from a middlebox consistent with proxy-termination.

Attachments: small pcap slice attached to internal thread (pcap_snapshot_20270914.zip)

Action items completed:
- I flagged the peer with our backbone team and requested immediate confirmation; they confirmed an automated route flap during a config push on peer-22.
- I requested rollback but the remote operator is investigating; they suggested a transient misconfiguration caused more specific routes to be suppressed, hence detour.

Next: recommend we temporarily remove the affected egress IP from the pool and push TTL flushes to resolvers for impacted prefixes while remote peer stabilizes.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com, Alex Kim <alex.kim@citrine.ai>, Citrine SRE <sre@citrine.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency + 502 spike — exec summary + next steps

Summary for execs and customer:
- Impact: Citrine Labs saw a 7% spike in 502 errors and >10x p99 tail latency (up to ~1.4s) during 08:44–09:10 PDT affecting ~12% of their requests.
- Root cause (interim): Automated config push on secondary peer (peer-22) caused transient route suppression. That suppression diverted a subset of traffic through an alternative transit that included a corporate proxy/middlebox producing TCP RSTs and variable NAT behavior, leading to 502s and tail latencies.
- Mitigation applied (09:18 PDT): we removed the suspect egress IP from rotation, pushed DNS TTL flushes to downstream resolvers, and coordinated with our backbone operator to restore peer announcements. Errors dropped back to baseline by 09:34 PDT for most users.

Outstanding items:
- Confirm full rollback and stable route announcements from the remote backbone operator (blocked until they confirm config resolution).
- Work with Citrine to validate client-side resolver caching behavior and advise a short client-side retry/backoff for transient 502s.
- Internal: add guardrails to prevent config pushes on peer-22 during peak windows and implement automated anomaly detection on route withdrawals.

Attachments included earlier (pcap + logs).
Doc links: JIRA-INF-4591 (tracking follow-up), internal notes: https://drive.redwood.internal/notes/citrine-0914

I'm escalating to Marcus (VP Eng) for awareness and potential SLA outreach if Citrine requests credits. Marcus — cc'ing you here. If anyone from leadership wants a short exec brief, I can prepare a one-pager.

- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Network & Edge, Redwood Inference
